findings.reason: naming the surface and its liveness filter decides whether §5's write paths are sufficient, and an unnamed query is exactly what lets a worker reach outside them.
findings.text: §5 says the script "asks reckon which projects have live runs owned by its owner's session", but no `reckon` command answers that question: `crew view live` refuses without `--project` (`{"error": "missing_project"}`) and `crew follow` requires `--project`, while the live pointer directory is not a live-run set (a pointer sampled there carried `phase: "complete"`). §5's write paths are the plugin script and its test only, so the worker must either pick an unnamed scan whose liveness filter the plan never states, or add Python query surface outside its scope — and the done-when stubs `reckon`, so the test cannot tell which it did

findings.reason: the further writes must be sequenced before the exec, so a node implementing the sentence literally builds a script that follows one project where two are live and fails the case the section declares.
findings.text: §5 orders the mechanism "execs the host at once with that project's request as the first request; each further project is written to the FIFO", but `exec` replaces the shell (script lines 63–67) so nothing after it runs in that process; the second project is never written and §5's own second case cannot be satisfied as written

findings.reason: a worker following the text applies the control to the wrong assertion and can record the third case's control as satisfied without ever falsifying the census substitution in the fourth.
findings.text: §3's third negative control reads "testing the session-wide attachment returns True in the third case", but the third case is now the hand-off, which touches no attachment reading; the control belongs to the fourth case, "an ask for the calling session while another host's follower is attached, and the calling host's census has no child", which is the only case that distinguishes `watch_state(...)["session_attached"]` from `_session_host_child_pid`

findings.reason: the edge delays §5 behind §3 without misdirecting any work, so it costs wall clock but sends no node down a wrong path.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` makes §5 wait on §3, and §5 repeats "It reads §3's ownership rule, so it waits for §3", but §5 changes only `plugins/crew-host/bin/crew-host`, which writes to the FIFO of the owner's own Claude process and never calls `_request_host_follower` or any other symbol §3 changes; §5's requests are owner-scoped by construction
